title: Preemptible Workload: Graceful Handback and Notification Playbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the automated and operator-driven behavior for graceful handback of preemptible workloads on the Redwood inference platform and the notification choreography for oncall and downstream teams. It covers detection signals, automated steps performed by the preemption-coordinator, operator run steps, verification, and post-incident artifacts.

Goals:
- Minimize user-visible errors when a node/GPU is revoked.
- Ensure 95% of preemptible workload handbacks complete without user-side failed requests (target: <= 5% error delta) during preemption windows.
- Ensure operators receive actionable alerts (context, tenant ID, model, active KV cache size) within 30s of preemption start.

Scope:
- Applies to workloads labeled: "preemptible", "spot", and bulk-batch inference jobs that accept transient placement.
- Applies to runtime components: serving-runtime, preemption-coordinator, allocator, kv-cache-service, and edge-request-proxy.
- Excludes dedicated-guaranteed capacity and admin-only maintenance drain operations.

Key definitions:
- Preemption event: A node/GPU is marked for revocation by the cloud provider or scheduler (internal signal: preemption.v1).
- Graceful handback: Sequence where serving-runtime completes or migrates in-flight KV cache + inflight requests before eviction.
- Handback window: Time budget allocated to a workload to finish or checkpoint (default: 25s for interactive, 120s for batch).

Ownership and contacts:
- Owner team: engineering (eng-platform/allocator and eng-serving-runtime).
- Primary oncall: platform-oncall (Slack: #platform-pager).
- Escalation: Oncall -> Senior Platform Engineer (pager duty) -> Head of Platform (email/pager).

SLOs and thresholds:
- Handback success rate (per-day): >= 95% (measured as requests completing within handback window without 5xx).
- Alert thresholds:
  - Alert A (Immediate): >1 preemption events/region resulting in >10% request error increase in 2m window -> Pager.
  - Alert B (Informational): Any preemption with KV cache size >1GB checkpointed -> Slack message to #platform-ops.

Signals and telemetry to monitor (example metrics):
- preemption.events.total (counter)
- runtime.handback.duration.p50/p95/p99 (histograms)
- runtime.handback.success_rate (gauge, 0-1)
- kvcache.checkpoint.size_bytes (gauge)
- tenant.request.error_rate (by-tenant label)

Automated policy (preemption-coordinator):
1. Receive cloud preemption signal (provider webhook / internal allocator preemption API).
2. Map affected pods/tasks -> tenant / model id -> attach operator context.
3. If workload.type == "interactive" then set handback_window=25s; else if workload.type == "batch" then handback_window=120s.
4. Instruct serving-runtime to:
   - Stop accepting new requests (drain strategy: 2s graceful window).
   - Snapshot KV cache to nearest warm store (S3/GCS) with prefix: s3://redwood-kv-backups/{tenant}/{model}/{timestamp}.
   - Attempt live KV streaming to sibling node in same region if network and resource permits (best-effort fallback).
5. Emit structured event: preemption.handback.started with payload (tenant, model, session_id, kv_size_bytes, handback_window).
6. If handback completes early, emit preemption.handback.completed; otherwise preemption.handback.timed_out and trigger model-variant-fallback.

Operator runbook (when automated flow fails or alert pages someone):
1. Triage from PagerDuty: read alert message, click runbook link, collect context (tenant ID, model name, node id, region).
2. Check aggregate metrics: run in Grafana: dashboard "Preemption — handback overview".
3. Check logs for preemption-coordinator and serving-runtime:
   - kubectl -n runtime logs deploy/preemption-coordinator --since=15m
   - kubectl -n runtime logs deploy/serving-runtime-{pod} --since=30m
4. If KV checkpoint failed and kv_size > 500MB:
   - Trigger manual checkpoint: kubectl exec -it {pod} -- /bin/sh -c '"/usr/local/bin/kv-checkpoint --dest s3://redwood-kv-backups/{tenant}/{model}/{ts} --force"'
   - Post a note in Slack thread with link to S3 object.
5. If requests are actively erroring and serving-runtime is unresponsive:
   - Initiate emergency-model-swap (see below) to a model-variant with no KV dependency.
   - Command: rcli model swap --tenant {tenant} --from {model} --to {model}-stateless-aug2026 --reason "preemption emergency"
6. If a tenant's tail latency rises >2x and cannot be mitigated: temporarily route tenant to dedicated pool (if entitlement) or apply soft-rate-limit: rcli tenant set-rate --tenant {tenant} --max-qps 0.5
7. Close the incident in status tool and populate postmortem template if handback success_rate < 90%.

Emergency model swap (short recipe):
- Preconditions: a stateless replica of the model exists in the catalog (tag: stateless-fallback).
- Steps:
  1. Lock routing for tenant: rcli routing lock --tenant {tenant} --reason preemption-swap
  2. Swap: rcli model swap --tenant {tenant} --from {model} --to {model}-stateless-fallback
  3. Monitor: the routing change should complete within 15s; ensure error rate decays to baseline within 60s.
  4. If swap fails, revert with: rcli model swap --tenant {tenant} --to {model} --force

Alert templates (Slack / PagerDuty):
- PagerDuty payload (example):
  title: "[PAGER] Preemption cascade — {region} — {tenant}"
  severity: critical
  details: "preemption.id={id} node={node} kv_size_bytes={kv} handback_window={window}s errors={err_percent}%"
- Slack ephemeral message to #platform-ops:
  "Preemption handback started: tenant={tenant} model={model} kv_size={kv_mb}MB handback_window={window}s — <link to dashboard>"

Configuration examples:
- Preemption policy YAML (applied to allocator):

apiVersion: redwood/v1
kind: PreemptionPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-interactive
spec:
  workloadType: interactive
  handbackWindowSeconds: 25
  drainGraceSeconds: 2
  maxKvCheckpointBytes: 1073741824 # 1GB
  fallbackModelTag: stateless-fallback

- Alert rule example (Prometheus-style pseudo YAML):
alert: PreemptionCascadeCritical
expr: increase(preemption.events.total[2m]) > 1 and increase(tenant.request.errors[2m]) / increase(tenant.requests[2m]) > 0.10
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Preemption cascade causing elevated errors"
  runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/preemptible-workload-graceful-handback-and-notification-playbook-2026.json"

Testing and validation checklist (pre-deploy):
- Synthetic preemption tests:
  1. Simulate provider preemption: ri preemption simulate --region us-west2 --count 3
  2. Validate events emitted in event store: rcli events query --type preemption.handback.started --since 5m
  3. Validate KV checkpoint presence in backup bucket and that object size matches reported kv_size_bytes.
- Canary rollout matrix: run simulation against 10% of interactive tenants for 24 hours, confirm handback_success_rate >= 97%.

Post-incident and retrospective guidance:
- Required when handback_success_rate < 90% for a day: full incident postmortem with action items, owner assignment, and a re-test plan.
- Collect artifacts: Grafana dashboard export, preemption-coordinator logs, serving-runtime traces, sample request traces for failed requests, S3 checkpoint links.
- Suggested retrospective topics:
  - Are handback windows sized appropriately by workload type?
  - Is KV checkpoint bandwidth sufficient?
  - Should we add automatic live KV streaming (cost vs. complexity)?

Observability improvements (backlog suggestions):
- Add taggable links in PagerDuty payload to the tenant route and recent traces.
- Instrument per-tenant checkpoint duration and upstream fallback latency.
- Add a derived dashboard panel showing "requests saved by graceful handback" vs "requests failed due to preemption".

Runbook maintenance and follow-up:
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime (rotating quarterly).
- Review cadence: every 6 months or after any preemption-related major incident.
- To propose changes: PR against docs repo, include test results from synthetic preemption test harness.

Appendix A — Example commands and quick references:
- Simulate preemption: ri preemption simulate --region eu-west1 --node-id node-abc123
- Check quota and backup bucket: aws s3 ls s3://redwood-kv-backups/{tenant}/{model}/ --human-readable
- Force checkpoint (pod exec): kubectl -n runtime exec {pod} -- /usr/local/bin/kv-checkpoint --dest s3://redwood-kv-backups/{tenant}/{model}/{ts} --force

Appendix B — Change log:
- 2025-11-12: Created by Aisha Kapoor (initial draft).
- 2026-01-15: Updated thresholds and added emergency-mode-swap recipe (reviewers: Diego, Priya).
- 2026-02-03: Published with Grafana dashboard links and Prometheus alert example.

Related artifacts and links:
- Dashboard: Grafana -> Preemption — handback overview (grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/preemption-handback)
- Synthetic harness: gitlab.redwood/inference/tests/preemption-harness
- Event schema: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/preemption-event-schema-2025.json

If you are the operator oncall: follow the Operator runbook steps above and run the post-incident checklist before clearing the alert. If unsure, escalate immediately to the senior platform engineer on rotation.
